learningObjective: Quantify how batch size increases arithmetic intensity from GEMV to GEMM regime for weight-shared linear layers.

canonicalClaims.claim: For a linear layer Y = X · W with weight W streamed once per launch, arithmetic intensity is approximately linear in the batch/token dimension B while the weight-byte term dominates, transitioning from GEMV-like (AI ≈ 1) at B = 1 to compute-bound (AI ≫ ridge) at moderate B on modern GPUs.
conditions: Weight W is streamed once from HBM per launch (no persistent-kernel weight caching).
AI measured against HBM bytes moved.
B remains small enough that the weight term still dominates bytes moved.
nonImplications: Does not imply AI grows without bound; large B eventually shifts bytes-moved toward activations.
Does not imply achieving compute-bound classification automatically yields peak throughput.

sourceMappings.locator: GEMV/GEMM transition, batching effect on AI

misconceptions.claim: Arithmetic intensity decreases with batch size because more activations traverse HBM.
misconceptions.whyWrong: In small-B regimes the weight bytes dominate; FLOPs scale with B while weight bytes are constant, so AI increases with B.

misconceptions.claim: AI is invariant in B because FLOPs and bytes both scale linearly with B.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Weight bytes are B-independent for a shared weight; only activation bytes scale with B. Overall bytes = O(K·N + B·(K+N)), giving AI ≈ B while the K·N term dominates.

misconceptions.claim: Larger batches always push into the compute-bound regime.
misconceptions.whyWrong: For very small K or N, or when W does not dominate bytes moved, batching alone may not cross the ridge point.

implementationFacts: AI ≈ (2·B·K·N) / (2·K·N + 4·B·K) for K=N linear layer FP16.
For K=N=4096: AI ≈ B while B ≪ K/2; crosses A100 FP16 ridge (~156) around B ~ 200.
performanceScenarios: LLM decode (B=1 per request) is GEMV-like; prefill (B = many tokens) is GEMM-like. Continuous batching in serving systems raises effective B to move decode into GEMM regime.
